title: Publishing a site at its Tracy address: one operation at a time, the flag only after the host's job is done and said so, no way round go-live, an unconfirmed operation held until its real outcome, and no button a role would be refused — and, since part 2, the site's own domain through the same operation: DNS shown only as measured, cleanups recorded half done and continued under the same key, and operations nobody reads settled in the background — and, since the review after #988, no bare domain reserved for ever, no name held without proof past 72 hours, and the site-connect-domain switch closing the doors that start an own domain
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout, with no database: env -u TEST_DATABASE_URL node --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-host/test/site-publish.test.mjs apps/tracy-host/test/run.test.mjs packages/fleet/tracy-fleet-operation/test/teardown-ingress.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/site-settings.test.mjs packages/core/tracy-core/test/site-publish-dom.test.mjs packages/site/tracy-my-sites/test/site-publish-dom.test.mjs packages/site/tracy-my-sites/test/more-settings.test.mjs packages/core/tracy-core/test/settings-rows.test.mjs — record EXIT1 = the exit code, and from the TAP summary FAIL1 = '# fail', SKIP1 = '# skipped'.

S2: With TEST_DATABASE_URL pointing at a PostgreSQL the run may create databases in: node --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-web/test/site-publish.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/sites-route.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/site-address.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/cron.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/ops-ui.test.mjs — record EXIT2, FAIL2, SKIP2 the same way. If no such PostgreSQL can be had, the verdict is BLOCKED (postgres), not PASS.

S3: In the output of S2 read the result line ('ok' or 'not ok') of the tests whose names start with: 'a double click, a second tab: two presses at once start ONE job' (GUARD); 'going live: 202 with the job, the flag stays draft while the job runs' (FLAG); 'roles: Owner and Admin publish and unpublish; Developer and Editor are refused' (ROLES); 'nobody signed in, a seat not yet accepted, a revoked seat, a stranger' (STRANGERS); 'the state door never moves the publish flag' (STATEDOOR); 'a request that carries `domains` is refused by name' (NODOMAINS); 'no answer from the host: nothing is called a success or a failure' (UNCONFIRMED); 'the answer that never arrived is found by asking again' (REASKED); 'a job the host calls done without the closing line of its script is not believed' (CLOSINGLINE); 'a job the host has no record of, failed because the host restarted, or ended on the site lock is NOT an ending' (NOOUTCOME); 'while the host cannot take the operation back' (HELD); 'the host says another job holds this site when a publish is pressed' (BUSY); 'the sweep hearing of a record that is no outcome does not end the operation either' (SWEEP); 'two reservations taken in the same millisecond are two operations' (SAMEMS); 'GET /settings while the address changes and a publish ends during the CMS read' (ONESNAPSHOT); 'job poll: a poll of an old build job after the site went live leaves the publish flag alone' (OLDPOLL); 'the state door reads every key before it writes' (STATEKEYS); 'an unresolved operation is resolved by the next read of the site' (ONREAD); 'GET /api/sites carries the operation under way' (LISTOP); 'a FRESH reservation whose door is still waiting on the host' (FRESHREAD); 'the host could not write `running`' (QUEUEDLOST); 'the host could not write `unobserved`' (RUNNINGLOST); 'a 4xx/5xx that is not the host' (UNVERIFIED); 'after the host ACCEPTED the job, no refusal ends the operation' (ACCEPTED); 'a door that died after reserving: the very next look hands the reservation to the host' (NOGRACE); 'the 202 is lost and the host changes while the script runs' (LOSTACK); 'the 202 is lost, the host restarts with the script still at work and has changed' (TAKENHELD); 'the ask never reached the host, and the host has changed' (NEVERTAKEN); 'the 202 is lost, the host restarts and its record of the job is deleted, damaged or unreadable' (RECORDLOST); 'the 202 is lost and the host can no longer LOOK AT its mark for the key' (MARKUNREAD); 'the host cannot write its mark for the key' (MARKWRITE).

S4: In the output of S1 read the result line of the tests whose names start with: 'one go-live per site: a second call while the first runs is refused GO_LIVE_BUSY' (HOSTGUARD); 'every malformed body is refused 400 before a job exists' (HOSTBODY); 'the same job key names the same job' (JOBKEY); 'a record that is no outcome is run again under the same key' (RERUN); 'go-live.sh: a required step that fails ends the script non-zero' (SCRIPTSTEPS); 'go-live.sh: Apache that takes neither a reload nor a restart' (SCRIPTAPACHE); 'go-live.sh: a firewall chain that cannot be READ ends the script' (FIREWALLREAD); 'go-live.sh beside another go-live of the same site ends at once with 75' (GOLIVELOCK); 'the address and the admin link come from the snapshot taken AFTER the CMS answered' (SNAPSHOTORDER); 'Editor and Developer: the state is shown, with no action at all' (EDITOR); 'reload in the middle of a publish: the tab opens on the running state' (RELOAD); 'a double click sends one request' (DOUBLE); 'the door took the press but the state after it cannot be read' (UNREAD); 'an operation the host has not confirmed: one line says the server is being waited for' (WAITING); 'another site picked while a quiet re-read of the first is pending' (SITESWITCH); 'an answer that names another site is not this site' (OTHERSITE); 'Back to draft says what really changes at a Tracy address' (DIALOG); 'a site published in ANOTHER browser tab' (OTHERTAB); 'a run that threw with its script still at work is no outcome' (UNOBSERVED); 'an ending the job store could not write is no outcome either' (STORELOST); 'go-live.sh live: a firewall check that could not be made is not "no rule"' (FIREWALLCHECK); 'while a publish runs on a site its row reads Publishing…' (ROWPUBLISHING); 'two reads of the list answered in reverse order' (LISTORDER); 'a snapshot that does not name its site is never drawn' (NAMELESS); 'every refusal this door gives is on the web door' (REFUSALLIST); 'a key the host has taken is answered with its job BEFORE the folder, the configuration or the request are checked' (KEYFIRST); 'a taken key whose record is no outcome, on a host that cannot run it again' (TAKENSAID); 'two asks for one key that arrive together with the folder vanishing between them' (KEYTURN); 'a job store that cannot be READ is not "never taken"' (STOREUNREAD); 'a key the host took, whose record is then lost, on a host that has changed' (MARKED); 'the mark is on disk before the record is written' (MARKFIRST); 'a mark that cannot be written: the key is NOT taken' (MARKFAIL); 'a mark that cannot be LOOKED AT is neither yes nor no' (MARKUNKNOWN); 'no mark and no record: the key was never taken' (NOMARK).

S5 (part 2): in the output of S2 read the result line of the tests whose names start with: 'Check DNS: each record reads what the lookup returned' (DNSREAD); 'a lookup that comes back after the name was removed' (LATELOOKUP); 'a name that is not a bare domain is refused by every door' (BADNAMES); 'only the Owner connects, checks or removes a domain' (TOKENOWNER); 'going live with an own domain DNS proves' (CARRIED); 'a domain DNS does not prove at the moment Publish is pressed is not carried' (NOTPROVEN); 'a cleanup that half succeeded is recorded as half done' (HALFDONE); 'removing a connected domain is an operation of the site' (REMOVEOP); 'two presses at the same moment are one operation' (ONEOP); 'a site is not deleted beside an operation of its own' (DELETEHELD); 'an operation whose door died after reserving it' (SWEEPSTART); 'no age ends, frees or drops an operation' (SWEEPAGE); 'a host that cannot be reached: the operation stays held and unconfirmed' (SWEEPBACKOFF); 'two replicas sweeping at the same moment' (SWEEPREPLICAS); 'the sweep takes a bounded batch' (NOAUTORETRY); 'a day of silence about a running job: the follow-up book does NOT give its row up' (FOLLOWUPKEPT).

S6 (part 2): in the output of S1 read the result line of the tests whose names start with: 'no tunnel configuration: publish and back to draft at the Tracy address still run' (NOTUNNEL); 'no tunnel configuration: only an ask that NAMES a domain is refused 501' (TUNNELONLY); 'a run that a signal, a time limit or a failed start ended is NOT the script failing' (SIGNAL); 'end to end with the real runner: a go-live script killed by a signal' (SIGNALREAL); 'runScript: a child ended by a signal has NO exit code' (RUNSIGNAL); 'a cleanup that failed is run again under its own key only when the next attempt is asked for' (ATTEMPT); 'drop-domain is a job like any other go-live' (DROPJOB); 'POST /_host/routing-target: the tunnel' (TARGETDOOR); 'go-live.sh: a record of domains that cannot be trusted is NOT "no domains"' (LEDGER); 'go-live.sh draft: the names it is given AND the ones on record leave the tunnel' (DRAFTPARTIAL); 'go-live.sh drop-domain: one domain out of the tunnel and off the record' (DROPSCRIPT); 'ingress_api.py: a write the provider says succeeded but does not show is a failure' (INGRESSBACK); 'ingress_api.py: every answer that is not the provider saying "success"' (INGRESSANSWERS); 'ingress_api.py --only-port' (ONLYPORT); 'the operation moving is told to the rest of the page' (EVENTOP); 'a publish that FAILED is told too' (EVENTFAIL); 'every state of an own domain has its screen' (DOMSTATES); 'each record says what to create and what the last lookup found there' (DOMRECORDS); 'nothing reads verified by inference' (NOINFER); 'a seat that is not the Owner sees the domain and its state' (DOMROLES).

S7 (review of part 2): in the output of S1 read the result line of the tests whose names start with: 'go-live.sh: a domain is said to be out only when its rule AND its place on the record are' (BOTHHALVES); 'go-live.sh: the record is never written through what was put beside it or under its name' (LEDGERWRITE); 'go-live.sh: a lock that cannot be taken' (LOCKKINDS); 'ingress_api.py: an add never takes over a rule that leads to another port' (ADDOWNED); 'ingress_api.py: an answer that does not SHOW the list of rules is not an empty list' (SHORTANSWER); 'ingress_api.py: an API base that is not an http(s) address, or a lock that is a link' (INGRESSLOCK); 'teardown through this door is an operation like the others' (TEARDOWNKEYED); 'while a publish runs the chip reads Publishing…' (ROWDELETING). In the output of S2: 'a delete TAKES the site before the host is asked' (DELETETAKES); 'a teardown that FAILED, or ended without its own closing line, deletes nothing' (DELETEFAILED); 'a delete whose door is no longer there to hear it is finished with nobody on the screen' (DELETESWEPT); 'a process that hears the host finish a delete but cannot close the book only writes the mark' (DELETEMARK); 'DELETE /api/sites/:key: a teardown still running when the wait ends removes NOTHING' (DELETEPENDING); "DELETE /api/sites/:key: a teardown that failed says the script's verdict line" (DELETESAID); 'two Check DNS of one reservation that end in the other order than they began' (DNSORDER); 'a body that carries a field its door does not take' (BODYSHAPE).

S8 (review after #988): in the output of S2 read the result line of the tests whose names start with: 'a bare (registrable) domain is refused by its own code' (APEX); 'a bare domain reserved before the refusal existed is not stuck' (APEXLEGACY); 'a reservation whose ownership was never proven stops holding the name after 72 hours' (LAPSE); 'a lapsed reservation can be made again by its holder' (RENEW); 'a reservation whose ownership was proven once is never taken away by age' (PROVENKEPT); 'a reading that arrives after the reservation lapsed proves nothing' (LATELAPSE); 'a Check DNS that found the TXT record and ended after a later one that did not' (PROOFORDER); 'a Check DNS that began before the deadline and waited for the row past it' (PROOFLOCK); 'a Check DNS that waits past the deadline behind a session that only LOCKED the row' (PROOFLOCKONLY); 'another site reserving a name while a session that only locked it holds it past the deadline' (TAKEOVERLOCK); 'the order reversed — a proof written before the deadline' (SWEEPWAIT); 'every name reserved before the server stopped taking it is not stuck' (LEGACYNAMES); 'the hourly sweep lets lapsed reservations go' (LAPSESWEEP); 'two sites taking the same lapsed name at once' (LAPSERACE); 'with the site-connect-domain switch off' (SWITCHOFF); 'a switch that cannot be read opens no door' (SWITCHUNREAD); 'a door that enforces a switch reads it strictly' (STRICTSWITCH). In the output of S1: 'a bare domain typed into Connect domain is refused under the field' (DOMAPEX); 'a bare domain reserved before it was refused: the card says why' (DOMAPEXLEGACY); 'a pending domain says until when it holds its name' (DOMLAPSED); 'Remove on a lapsed reservation clears its notice' (DOMLAPSEDREMOVE); 'a lapsed reservation is read only from the lapsed list' (PARSELAPSED); 'a pending bare domain reads `unsupported`' (PARSEAPEX); 'a bare domain reserved before it was refused, whose publish failed' (DOMAPEXFAILED); 'a name under a suffix the server cannot tell is a registered one' (DOMUNCONNECTABLE).
expect: GUARD, FLAG, ROLES, STRANGERS, STATEDOOR, NODOMAINS, UNCONFIRMED, REASKED, CLOSINGLINE, NOOUTCOME, HELD, BUSY, SWEEP, SAMEMS, ONESNAPSHOT, OLDPOLL, STATEKEYS, ONREAD, LISTOP, FRESHREAD, QUEUEDLOST, RUNNINGLOST, UNVERIFIED, ACCEPTED, NOGRACE, LOSTACK, TAKENHELD, NEVERTAKEN, RECORDLOST, MARKUNREAD and MARKWRITE are each 'ok' (before this change: the door answered 200 with publish 'published' as soon as the host took the job, two presses started two jobs, the state door set the flag by itself, and any domain in the body reached the host).

HOSTGUARD, HOSTBODY, JOBKEY, RERUN, SCRIPTSTEPS, SCRIPTAPACHE, FIREWALLREAD, GOLIVELOCK, SNAPSHOTORDER, EDITOR, RELOAD, DOUBLE, UNREAD, WAITING, SITESWITCH, OTHERSITE, DIALOG, OTHERTAB, UNOBSERVED, STORELOST, FIREWALLCHECK, ROWPUBLISHING, LISTORDER, NAMELESS, REFUSALLIST, KEYFIRST, TAKENSAID, KEYTURN, STOREUNREAD, MARKED, MARKFIRST, MARKFAIL, MARKUNKNOWN and NOMARK are each 'ok'.

DNSREAD, LATELOOKUP, BADNAMES, TOKENOWNER, CARRIED, NOTPROVEN, HALFDONE, REMOVEOP, ONEOP, DELETEHELD, SWEEPSTART, SWEEPAGE, SWEEPBACKOFF, SWEEPREPLICAS, NOAUTORETRY, FOLLOWUPKEPT are each 'ok' (before part 2: no domain reached the host, a domain read ready from one stored flag with no word on what was looked up, nothing swept an operation nobody read, and a go-live follow-up was dropped after a day).

NOTUNNEL, TUNNELONLY, SIGNAL, SIGNALREAL, RUNSIGNAL, ATTEMPT, DROPJOB, TARGETDOOR, LEDGER, DRAFTPARTIAL, DROPSCRIPT, INGRESSBACK, INGRESSANSWERS, ONLYPORT, EVENTOP, EVENTFAIL, DOMSTATES, DOMRECORDS, NOINFER, DOMROLES are each 'ok' (before part 2: every go-live answered 501 on a host with no tunnel configuration, a script killed by a signal was recorded as exit code 1, a failed cleanup could only be answered with the failure it had, and the publish event fired only when the flag moved).

BOTHHALVES, LEDGERWRITE, LOCKKINDS, ADDOWNED, SHORTANSWER, INGRESSLOCK, TEARDOWNKEYED, ROWDELETING, DELETETAKES, DELETEFAILED, DELETESWEPT, DELETEMARK, DELETEPENDING, DELETESAID, DNSORDER, BODYSHAPE are each 'ok' (before the review round: a removal was said before the record was rewritten; an add replaced a rule that led to another port; a short provider answer read as an empty list; the delete door looked for an operation and then erased the row whatever the teardown did; two lookups could land in either order; unknown body fields were dropped).

APEX, APEXLEGACY, LAPSE, RENEW, PROVENKEPT, LATELAPSE, PROOFORDER, PROOFLOCK, PROOFLOCKONLY, TAKEOVERLOCK, SWEEPWAIT, LEGACYNAMES, LAPSESWEEP, LAPSERACE, SWITCHOFF, SWITCHUNREAD, STRICTSWITCH, DOMAPEX, DOMAPEXLEGACY, DOMAPEXFAILED, DOMUNCONNECTABLE, DOMLAPSED, DOMLAPSEDREMOVE, PARSELAPSED and PARSEAPEX are each 'ok' (before the review fix, on c999b8370: `PUT …/address {name: 'example.com', kind: 'custom'}` answered 202; a reservation aged 73 hours still answered another site NAME_TAKEN, and neither the sweep nor a reserve let it go; with `site-connect-domain` off, reserving answered 409/202 instead of 403 OWN_DOMAIN_DISABLED).

selectors.workingLine: [data-section='domains'] [data-working] (data-confirmed='false' while the host has not confirmed)
selectors.goLiveDoor: POST /api/sites/:key/go-live ({op} only; `domains` → 400 DOMAINS_NOT_SUPPORTED; `live` carries the own domains DNS proves when it is pressed)
selectors.stateDoor: GET /api/sites/:key/state · POST /api/sites/:key/state (plan only; `publish` → 409 PUBLISH_BY_GO_LIVE; any other field → 400 INVALID_REQUEST)
selectors.settingsDoor: GET /api/sites/:key/settings (siteUrl, adminUrl, currentSiteUrl, addressChange, publishing: one snapshot)
selectors.hostDoor: POST /_host/go-live ({label, op: live|draft|drop-domain|teardown, jobKey, domains?, routingTarget?, attempt?}; a body that is not a JSON object, or a field that is there with the wrong type (null included) → 400; the tunnel configuration is asked for only when `domains` is not empty)
selectors.ownDomainCard: [data-card='own-domain'] (data-domain-state: waiting | wrong | unknown | verified | connecting | live | connected | failed | removing | cleanup | unsupported | lapsed)
selectors.domainActions: [data-action='check-dns'|'connect-live'|'remove-domain'|'retry-remove'|'reserve-again'] (check-dns and reserve-again hidden too by the UI switch site-connect-domain)
selectors.removeDomainDoor: DELETE /api/sites/:key/address/domain ({name}; 200 for a reservation, 202 for an operation `drop-domain`)
selectors.deleteDoor: DELETE /api/sites/:key (200 {removed: true, host: true, …} once the host said the site is gone; 409 TEARDOWN_FAILED with the row kept; 202 DELETE_PENDING; 409 PUBLISH_BUSY while another operation holds the site)
selectors.fieldError: form[data-form='domain'] [data-line='field-error'] (a refusal of what was typed, under the field: settings.url.apex names www.<domain>)
selectors.holdUntilLine: [data-card='own-domain'] [data-line='hold-until'] (data-hold-until: until when a pending domain holds its name unproven)
selectors.reserveDoor: PUT /api/sites/:key/address ({name, kind: custom}; 400 DOMAIN_APEX_UNSUPPORTED {name, suggestion}; 403 OWN_DOMAIN_DISABLED; 503 UI_SETTING_UNREADABLE; 202 pending.holdUntil)

evidence: Before the change (base e5aecf517, origin/develop with nothing of this change): the new and changed test files run against the base sources exit 1 — 85 of 102 fail, 61 of them behaviour assertions (the door answered 200/published at once, no PUBLISH_BUSY, the state door set the flag, a body with domains reached the host, a host body of `null` answered 500, a failed required step of go-live.sh still ended 0, the Settings address was worked out before the CMS read, no chip, no Publish button). Review after #988 (base c999b8370): the eleven new tests of site-address.test.mjs run against the base sources on a PostgreSQL of the run: 8 fail by their own assertions — `example.com at PUT /address: 202 !== 400`; an aged reservation still held (`409 !== 202` for the second site); the switch off still answered `409 !== 403`; the sweep let nothing go — and the guard that a proven name is never taken passes on both trees.
fence: apps/tracy-web: site_publish_op reservation with its own ref (069-site-publish-op.sql, publish-store.js reservePublishOp — one statement; going back to draft, the reservation and the lowered flag in one transaction, so no read sees the operation while the site still reads published), every write about an operation conditional on that ref, settleGoLive (the flag only from an ended job that printed its closing line for this site and direction; a record that is no outcome — gone, failed by a restart, ended on the lock, or without its script's exit code (scriptOutcome: done needs exit code 0, failed needs the script's non-zero one) — never ends it; nothing sweeps such an operation in the background, every read of the site asks the host again under the same key), publish.js (role before body, `domains` refused by name, every read asking the host again under the same job key for every operation without an outcome — a fresh `starting`, a job the host shows queued or running, a lost or orphaned record — with no grace period, 'busy' is not an outcome, an operation ended as refused only on the host's own refusal (publish-store.js HOST_REFUSALS: the code and its status) that also says the host never took the operation's key (`accepted: false`) — a row without a job id is not that proof, the state door refusing `publish` and any field beside `plan` before it writes), seats/route.js (the list carries the operation under way), settings.js + route.js (the address, the admin link, the address state and the publishing state read in one repeatable-read snapshot after the CMS answered and after any ending was written), the build-job poll no longer naming the publish flag. apps/tracy-host: goLiveRoute (object body, per-site guard, job key looked up before the configuration, the label and the site folder are checked, one key's asks answered in turn, every refusal to a keyed ask saying whether the key was taken — read from a durable acceptance mark (jobs.js acceptJob / jobAccepted: `<id>.accepted`, synced before the record, the script and the 202; present → `accepted: true` even with the record gone, damaged or unreadable; path absent → `accepted: false`; mark not readable → no `accepted`; mark not writable → 503 and nothing taken), never from the record being absent; a record that is no outcome is run again under the same key — hasOutcome), runGoLiveJob (an ending is recorded with the script's exit code or as `unobserved` with none), exit 75 recorded as busy. packages/fleet: go-live.sh — every step of the mail and noindex switches ends the script non-zero when it fails, one go-live per site by a kernel lock (exit 75), and `iptables -C` read three ways (0 there, 1 absent, anything else a check that did not happen). Client: usePublishing reads the state back after every press; a snapshot is drawn only for the site it was asked for and names (one that names none is never drawn); My Sites writes Publishing… and withholds "Publish…" while an operation runs, and applies only the latest read of its list; data-status / data-action / data-working / data-confirmed / data-line attributes. PART 2 — apps/tracy-web: 070-site-own-domain.sql; address.js (a bare-name grammar for own domains, one lookup per record kept as measured — status, observed, error, time on the database clock — and bound to the reservation's token and the host's target, the token sent to the Owner alone, removal of a routed domain as an operation); publish-store.js (reservation under the site's names lock, domains chosen from a reading taken for that publish, `carried_at`, settleGoLive reading the script's per-domain lines, a failed cleanup recorded half done and taken back under its own ref with the next attempt); publish.js (createPublisher shared by the doors and the sweep, sweepHeld on the database clock with skip-locked batches and a bounded back-off, never ending anything by age); door-follow-up.js (a go-live row is never dropped after a day); route.js (the delete door refuses while an operation holds the site). apps/tracy-host: run.js (a signal or a failed start has no exit code), goLiveRoute (the tunnel asked for only when a domain is named, `drop-domain`, `routingTarget`, `attempt` via hasOutcomeFor, a domain grammar equal to the ledger's), runGoLiveJob (signal / time limit recorded as unobserved), POST /_host/routing-target. packages/fleet: lib/site-lifecycle.sh (one lock for go-live and teardown, the ledger read once and refused when it cannot be trusted), go-live.sh (ledger written before the rule, `--only-port`, non-zero while a domain is left), ingress_api.py (one lock per tunnel, read back after every write, nothing written that is already so, every answer that is not `success` refused), teardown.sh (the door closed before the data goes). Client: readPublishing takes `drop-domain`, domainState, OwnDomainCard, SITE_PUBLISH_EVENT on every move of the operation. REVIEW AFTER #988 — apps/tracy-web: address.js `ownable` (tldts, ICANN part of the public suffix list: a registrable domain itself → DOMAIN_APEX_UNSUPPORTED with `www.` of it; a public suffix or unknown suffix → INVALID_SITE_KEY; removal parses with `heldCandidate`, which takes any name a site may hold), `LAPSED` / `releaseLapsed` (077-site-own-domain-hold.sql: hold_until 72 h on the database clock, ownership_proven_at never cleared by a later lookup, site_name_lapse notices; one CTE deletes the lapsed row and writes the notice; the reserve door releases before its insert, the unique name decides a race; writeReading refuses a lapsed row), `startClosed` (ui-setting.js `uiSwitchOn`, a strict reader: off → 403 OWN_DOMAIN_DISABLED on reserve/verify/availability of a custom domain, unreadable → 503 UI_SETTING_UNREADABLE); cron.js sweepExpired releases lapsed reservations. Client: settings-rows (state `lapsed`, `problem`, `holdUntil`; DomainState `lapsed`/`unsupported`), SiteDomains (the refusal under the field, the lapsed and unsupported cards, Reserve again), refusals.ts (the three codes on their own statuses), catalogue.json text, site-tabs-rules.css (the switch hides Check again and Reserve again too).
